newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian premier rules out Chechen independence.
newsitem.headline: Russian premier rules out Chechen independence.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday ruled out granting full independence to breakaway Chechnya and said third parties should not interfere in the long-running conflict.

"Russia's territorial integrity, its borders -- including internal ones -- the provisions of Russia's constitution are not up for bargaining," Chernomyrdin told the Federation Council upper house of parliament. "Chechnya is Russia's internal affair. There should be no doubt about that."

Chernomyrdin praised the peace deal struck by security chief Alexander Lebed with Chechen separatists on August 31 but made clear the accord, which ended 21 months of fighting, was not a proper legal document.
"There have been no agreements on Chechnya, no one has signed any agreements," Chernomyrdin said. "There has been a framework of political declarations."
Chernomyrdin said Moscow saw its main aim in Chechnya now as establishing a basis for a peaceful settlement.
He said Russia would focus on helping to set up a regional administration, demilitarising the region, rebuilding its social structures and preparing for free and fair elections.
